parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The value of the solubility product, $K_{sp}$, of iron(III) hydroxide, $\text{Fe(OH)}_3$, is given by the following expression.

$$K_{sp} = [\text{Fe}^{3+}][\text{OH}^-]^3 = 2.0 \times 10^{-39}\ \text{mol}^4\ \text{dm}^{-12}$$

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the solubility of $\text{Fe(OH)}_3$ in water.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the solubility of $\text{Fe(OH)}_3$ in $0.010\ \text{mol dm}^{-3}$ barium hydroxide, $\text{Ba(OH)}_2\text{(aq)}$.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
$\text{Fe(OH)}_3$ is less soluble in $\text{Ba(OH)}_2\text{(aq)}$ than it is in pure water.

Name this effect.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The numerical value of the $K_a$ of $\text{HBrO}$ is $2.00 \times 10^{-9}$.

$\mathbf{X}$ is a solution of $\text{HBrO}$ which contains $4.00 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{mol}$ of $\text{HBrO}$ in $100\ \text{cm}^3$ of solution. In this solution the following equilibrium is established in which there are two conjugate acid-base pairs. $$\text{HBrO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{BrO}^- + \text{H}_3\text{O}^+$$

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Identify the two conjugate acid-base pairs shown in the equation above.

pair one acid base

pair two acid base

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the pH of solution $\mathbf{X}$. Show all your working.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
A solution containing $2.00 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{mol}$ of $\text{NaOH}$ is added to solution $\mathbf{X}$. A buffer solution is formed.

Calculate the pH of this buffer solution.
